title: Cache telemetry v2: dashboards + hit-rate regression alerts
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Build the Cache Telemetry v2 dashboard set + regression alerting for cache hit-rate effectiveness, with an explicit noise budget and clear runbook links.

Why
We are adding/standardizing v2 cache metrics (hit/miss/partial, hit-bytes, saved-prefill-ms, cacheable prompt ratio). Without a trustworthy dashboard + regression alerts, we won’t catch degradations during rollout (and we’ll keep getting confused customer questions like SUP-3921).

References
- Confluence dashboard definition: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cache-hit-rate-dashboards-definition.json
- Confluence alert proposal: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/cache-hit-rate-regression-alerting.json
- Data quality runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/cache-telemetry-data-quality-runbook.json
- Perf canary coverage: ENG-4819 (release gating signal; this ticket focuses on dashboards/alerts consumption)
- Observability pack PR (expected): sources/github/observability-pack/pr-921.json

Scope
1) Dashboards (Console / internal Grafana)
- Overview: global cache effectiveness
  - cache_hit_rate (definition per v2: hits / (hits + misses), with partial reported separately)
  - cache_hit_bytes and cache_miss_bytes
  - saved_prefill_ms (sum + per-request distribution)
  - cacheable_prompt_ratio (cacheable / total)
- Drilldowns:
  - by deployment_mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
  - by region
  - by model + model_version (with cardinality controls; see ADR-027)
  - by route (top-N only + hashed route bucket fallback when needed)
- Troubleshooting panels:
  - sampling_rate effective
  - dropped_tag_events / cardinality_guardrail_drops
  - partial_prefill_rate (to catch misclassification)

2) Alerts (SRE owned; telemetry support)
- Regression alert: cache_hit_rate drop
  - burn-rate style (fast/slow windows) to reduce sensitivity to traffic mix changes
  - segmented alerts: route + region (top routes only) and global/regional aggregate
  - gating/enablement: only for tiers/regions where v2 telemetry flag is enabled
- Regression alert: saved_prefill_ms drop (secondary corroboration)
  - catches “hit-rate stable but savings not realized” cases (misclassification or prefill path change)
- Data quality alert (non-paging): sudden increase in cardinality_guardrail_drops or missing required tags

Noise budget / acceptance criteria
- Paging alerts:
  - <= 2 pages/week across all cache telemetry alerts for the oncall rotation during staged rollout.
  - Alerts must include: impacted segment, likely causes checklist, and a direct link to runbook + relevant dashboard view.
- Non-paging notifications:
  - allowed higher volume but must be deduped (no more than 1 notification per 30 min per segment).

Definition details (must match v2 spec)
- cache_hit_rate should exclude requests with unknown outcome; unknown outcome should be separately charted.
- partial outcomes are not counted as hits; they should be charted + used to annotate overall effectiveness.
- saved_prefill_ms should be aggregated with consistent units and include sampling correction (if applicable).

Out of scope
- New UI polish beyond agreed dashboard layout
- ML-driven anomaly detection (use burn-rate thresholds + simple seasonality guard only if already available)

Rollout
- Dashboards can be deployed immediately but should be labeled “v2 (flagged)” until rollout reaches >= 3 regions.
- Alerts must be disabled by default and enabled during staged rollout only after telemetry pipeline validation passes.

Deliverables
- Observability-pack updates (dashboards + alert templates)
- SRE runbook links embedded in alert payloads
- Written threshold rationale + tuning notes (link in this ticket)

Owners / reviewers
- Primary: Sergio Costa
- SRE sign-off: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes
- Telemetry data validation: Logan Wright, Caleb Johnson
- Cardinality review: Thomas Baird
comments: 2025-02-12 (Sergio Costa): Drafted dashboard panel list aligned to Confluence definition. Waiting on final metric field names from ENG-4815 pipeline update so queries don’t get churned. In the meantime, using placeholders for: cache_hit_rate_v2, cache_hit_bytes_v2, saved_prefill_ms_v2, cacheable_prompt_ratio_v2.

2025-02-14 (Caleb Johnson): Heads-up: we are enforcing drop rules when route/model tags exceed budget; please make sure dashboards don’t rely on full-cardinality breakdown. Recommend: top-N routes + an ‘other’ bucket, plus a separate panel charting cardinality_guardrail_drops so folks don’t misinterpret missing series as ‘no traffic’.

2025-02-17 (Rafael Mendes): For paging, please avoid per-tenant segmentation. Route+region is enough for now; tenant-based paging will blow up oncall noise. Also need a clear runbook link for ‘hit-rate down’ that includes how to confirm if it’s traffic mix vs actual regression.

2025-02-18 (Sergio Costa): Implemented first pass in observability-pack branch: overview dashboard + drilldowns by deployment_mode/region. Added troubleshooting row: sampling_rate_effective and cardinality_guardrail_drops. Next: alert templates with burn-rate windows and gating on feature flag enablement tag.

2025-02-20 (Sean Gallagher): Proposed noise budget accepted (<=2 pages/week during rollout). Please stage alerts: start with non-paging notifications for 48h, then enable paging for global aggregate only, then add top routes once stable. Also confirm what constitutes ‘regression’: relative drop vs absolute threshold (recommend both).

2025-02-21 (Sergio Costa): Added burn-rate style alert draft: fast 15m / slow 2h windows, triggers when hit-rate drops >8% relative and crosses absolute threshold (configurable). Added annotation to include partial_prefill_rate so we can spot misclassification. Pending final review by Sean/Rafael.

2025-02-24 (Logan Wright): Please ensure the alert expression excludes outcome=unknown and surfaces unknown_rate as context. We’ve seen unknown spikes during partial-prefill edge cases (tracked in known issues page). Also, saved_prefill_ms alert should be ‘corroboration only’ (non-paging) until overhead/profiling is validated.
